headline: Indian markets reopen after holiday; OYO slashes IPO size while Flipkart reports record festive user engagement.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Indian markets are reopening after the Dussehra holiday observed on October 20.
Investors are reacting to a sharp market crash on Monday where the Sensex fell over 850 points.
Elevated crude oil prices and global inflation risks are weighing on investor sentiment.
Private banking and IT stocks led the recent market downturn, dragging down major indices.
whatHappening: OYO's parent company is nearly halving its IPO fresh issue size to up to ₹3,350 crore.
Flipkart hit a new high in daily active users during the start of the festive e-commerce season.
Newsprint manufacturers are seeking PM intervention to resolve a critical coal supply crisis.
US markets ended higher on Tuesday as healthcare gains offset a breather in technology stocks.
summary: Indian markets resume trading today following the Dussehra holiday and a significant 1,000-point Sensex crash on Monday. OYO has significantly reduced its IPO fresh issue target, while Flipkart reports record-breaking user engagement during the festive season. Global cues are mixed as US markets recovered on Tuesday despite ongoing concerns over oil prices and inflation.
